intro:
Use it under an assistant's answer to show the pages the answer was written from. Each page has a number, and `Sources.Citation` puts that number in the answer where the page is used. Point at a citation and its page lights up in the list, with a card of what the page says. Point at a page and its citations light up.

While the search runs, set `status="searching"` with the `query`. The line says what is being searched for, a ruler fills a tick for each page read, and pages still to come hold their place as empty cards, so the list does not jump. Once the list is final, set `status="done"` and the line reads "Read 5 sources".

The answer has to sit inside `Sources`, because that is how its citations find their pages. When the answer is a [Message](/docs/web/components/message), put `Sources` inside its content.
usage:
{pages.map((page) => ( ))}

Most often it is under-proofing .

parts.Trigger: The line over the list: the sites' icons, what is happening, a ruler with a tick for each page, and a chevron. Pressing it folds the list away. `icons` sets how many site icons it stacks, and `0` hides them.
parts.Content: The pages, numbered by their place. `layout="cards"`, the default, is a row of cards that scrolls sideways and snaps, with arrows and a fade at the end that has more. `layout="list"` is a column of single lines. While searching, it adds an empty card for each page still to come, up to `total`.
parts.Source: One page: its number, the site's icon and name, its `title` and a `snippet` of what it says. It opens `href` in a new tab. With no `icon`, the site's first letter is drawn on a tint picked from its name. `unreachable` keeps a page that could not be read in the list, marked, with its tick in the ruler turned red.
parts.Citation: A numbered mark in the answer that points at the source with that `index`. Pointing at it or focusing it lights the source and opens a card with its title and snippet. Pressing it opens the page.

examples.title: Folded until asked
examples.description: `defaultOpen={false}` keeps the list to one line until it is pressed. The citations still work while it is folded: point at one to read what its page says.

examples.title: As a list
examples.description: `layout="list"` gives each page one line: its number, its site, its title and its host. Use it where the pages are references rather than reading, such as documentation and issues. `icons={0}` leaves the site icons off the line.

examples.title: A page that could not be read
examples.description: `unreachable` keeps the page in the list, marked, and turns its tick in the ruler red, so a reader can tell a short answer from a search that partly failed.

notes:
### Where the pages come from

With the AI SDK, the pages are the `source-url` parts of an assistant message: `part.url` is the `href` and `part.title` the `title`. Remove duplicates by URL first, because a model may cite the same page twice. A part with no title falls back to the page's host.

### Numbers

A source is numbered by its place in `Sources.Content`, from 1. Pass `index` to number it yourself, for example when the model's citations already carry numbers.

### Accessibility

The trigger is a button with `aria-expanded`. Each source is a link that says it opens in a new tab, and each citation is named "Source 2: its title". The citation's card opens on focus as well as on hover.

### Reduced motion

With reduced motion turned on, the searching line does not shimmer, the ruler does not pulse, and the list folds without sliding.
